method: Actual v14 untimed challenge engine. Four original bosses (Ignis, Mime, Prism, Caden), +65 HP and automatic transition after each nonfinal boss; victory immediately after Caden. No encore, timeout, HP override or damage override. The 300-second guard belongs only to this offline test runner and never finishes the game state.
difficultyRevision: V14 keeps blade waves alternating with pursuit. Pursuit now has six single shots (.20 tracking/.65 lock/.25 flight,1.10s launch interval), three sequential pincer turns (.20/.65/.55,1.40s interval), and three simultaneous finale blades (.35 tracking/1.15 fixed warning/.85 flight). Ten locks and12 moving bodies;13.15 active seconds plus1.85 initial warning and.8 cinematic totals about15.8 seconds. A naturally completed takeover grants one1.8-second stopped-boss counter window with20 percent increased actual damage; cancelled casts grant none. Four new fifth normal patterns are light rehearsal, visibly marked silhouette choice, delayed replay of the real movement history, and three quick Encore slashes followed by a clearly warned late fourth. Original boss HP/QWER values and the previous normal attack geometry remain unchanged.
domainRule: The full initial warning follows the frozen cinematic. Caden alternates gap alignment against blade walls with reacting to pursuit lock cues and changing direction away from two aimed lanes. A reached pursuit destination is held until both blades pass; the next sequence tracks afresh. The finale launches three blades at once after its longer warning. A real survival counter window never changes the fatal collision rule. Preview lanes and cleared trails never damage. All actual takeover body contact is fatal despite HP, E guard, dodge or R attack protection; a committed R cinematic only pauses the world and cannot erase an active takeover.
bladeReactionMethod: 180 actual-step walks: both characters, three layouts and their mirrors, five player starts and three boss starts; .35-second input reaction after initial/relocation cues and the final diagonal turn. No dash, buff, attack, teleport, HP edit or invulnerability. 180 additional still/one-direction/circle policies test whether simple camping solves the sequence. The full challenge bots separately use .53/.29/.14-second reaction policies and ten-Hz decisions.
pursuitReactionMethod: 108 walks from nine arena starts, both characters, both boss phases and three boss positions with .35-second reactions on every tracking/lock cue. Repeated with .65-second reactions, with and without a real directional Space dash once per beat when available. 180 still/eight-fixed-directions/fixed-circle controls and18 controls that escape only the first beat then stop. No HP edits, teleport or damage immunity overrides. Full challenge bots keep existing profile delays and ten-Hz observation/decisions, including each new lock. Between decisions their60Hz motor control releases held movement at the already-observed target or outside the memorized locked lanes; it does not observe a new attack earlier. This avoids the old100ms motor overshoot artifact and is a controller revision, not an engine immunity or damage adjustment. Exposure counts are actual full-challenge casts/activations/completions, separate from isolated route tests. Run-time medians include the new2.0/2.2-second entry cinematics; these do not advance combat or cooldowns.

baselineComparison.source: Recorded v13 report before pursuit structure, fourth extra mechanics and counter windows. Same controller seeds and reaction policies; v14 adds policies for the visibly marked real silhouette and ordered rehearsal lights.

scoreRule: Actual HP damage × combo multiplier + 60 per landed JUST attack + 150 per JUST dodge. No overkill or clear bonus. Combo +0.25 per 8 hits (max 2.5), FEVER adds 0.5 (max 3).
takeoverRouteMethod: 40 actual-step walks from center and four corners across both characters; dodge cooldown stays unavailable. Eight additional tests start at the initial guide and remain still. No attack, HP override, invulnerability or teleport during traversal.
openingReactionMethod: Each new normal attack from a fixed open-arena position: stand still versus walk upward after 0.35 seconds, both fixed characters. No dodge or skill, no HP or damage override; initial spawn invulnerability is explicitly removed for this collider test.
purpleReactionMethod: Separate single-Purple open-arena scenarios: walk upward after the stated delay from the lock cue. No dodge or skills. These measure timing at one position, not human success rates.
limitations: Input controllers know visible hazard geometry, numbered light goals and the marked real silhouette; their win rates are not human win rates. The audition policy has a profile-dependent chance of choosing the visibly wrong figure.

Controllers use visible geometry and stop attacking during takeovers. New relocation warnings, the final diagonal turn, and pursuit tracking/lock transitions incur their profile reaction delay; initial warnings also require elapsed reaction time. These are geometry-aware policies, not calibrated human skill levels.
Profile differences are policies, not a calibrated human skill ordering; a middle policy can fare worse than a slower policy in some character matchups.
Victory and boss timing medians include completed fights only.
The 300-second simulation guard is a test safety measure; there is no time limit in the game.
Historical booth-balance-report.json measures the superseded timed mode and is not validation of this untimed challenge.
